column1: Glob vs regex: which is anchored by default?
column2:
GLOB = anchored: must match the WHOLE name; WIDEN with *.
REGEX = unanchored: matches a substring; PIN with ^ and $.
Same goal, opposite defaults.

  find . -name 'log'   -> "log" only  (log.txt / mylog fail)
  grep -E 'log'        -> any line containing "log"
  grep -E '^log$'      -> "log" only

column1: BRE vs ERE: who needs the backslash?
column2:
BRE (grep, sed default): the powerful metachars ? + { } ( ) | are LITERAL
  -> escape them to ACTIVATE:  \?  \+  \{ \}  \( \)  \|
ERE (grep -E, sed -E, bash [[ =~ ]]): they are special BY DEFAULT
  -> escape them to make LITERAL.
Opposite worlds. (\1 backreferences exist in BRE; not in POSIX ERE.)

column1: GitHub Actions: how do you exclude a file from a paths: trigger?
column2:
Add a !-prefixed negation AFTER the positive glob (last matching pattern wins).
You CANNOT mix `paths` and `paths-ignore` for one event.

  paths:
    - "apps/bot/**"
    - "!apps/bot/*.md"   # order matters: negation must follow the include

column1: GitHub Actions path filter: push touches an excluded doc AND a source file — run or skip?
column2:
RUNS. Filters evaluate the WHOLE changeset: if ANY changed file matches an
include (and isn't excluded), the workflow runs. The exclusion only skips
pushes that are EXCLUSIVELY excluded files. (A skipped push creates NO run.)

column1: GitHub Actions glob: what do ? and + mean (vs shell glob)?
column2:
Regex-style QUANTIFIERS on the preceding char, NOT shell wildcards:
  ? = zero-or-one of preceding,  + = one-or-more of preceding.
  e.g. *.jsx?  matches BOTH page.js AND page.jsx (trailing x optional).
Also: * doesn't cross /, ** does; patterns anchored to whole path from repo root.
No brace expansion: list **/*.ts and **/*.tsx separately (never **/*.{ts,tsx}).

column1: JS/TS regex: \1 in the pattern vs $1 in the replacement?
column2:
PATTERN: \1 = backreference — matches the SAME TEXT group 1 captured.
  /(\w)\1/ matches "ll" (a doubled char), NOT any two chars.
  Named: \k<name>.
REPLACEMENT string (.replace): use $1 (and $<name>) to INSERT the capture.
  \1 in a replacement is a literal, not a backref.

column1: JS/TS regex: what does a lookahead (?=...) / (?!...) do?
column2:
Zero-width ASSERTION: checks what FOLLOWS without consuming it (not part of match).
  /foo(?=bar)/ matches "foo" only if "bar" follows, but the match is just "foo".
  (?!...) = negative. Lookbehind (?<=...)/(?<!...) is the backward version (ES2018).
Stack them for independent AND conditions at the same spot:
  /(?=.*\d)(?=.*[a-z]).{8,}/  -> each (?=) peeks from the current position and rewinds.

column1: JS/TS regex: what causes catastrophic backtracking (ReDoS)?
column2:
A quantifier NESTED inside another over the same class: (a+)+, (a*)*, (a|a)+.
On input that ALMOST matches (e.g. a trailing char that fails a final $), the engine
tries exponentially many ways to split the run before failing -> hang.
Fix: flatten to a+ / a*, or anchor to remove the ambiguity.

column1: YAML: when must you quote a value (e.g. a GHA path pattern)?
column2:
When it STARTS with a syntax token, YAML reads it as that token, not text:
  *  = alias    &  = anchor    !  = tag    [ or { = flow collection   (? : - in places)
Unquoted -> parse error / mis-parse. Quote it -> literal string.

  - "!apps/**"     # ! -> tag without quotes
  - "*.md"         # * -> alias without quotes
  - "[a-z]*.ts"    # [ -> flow sequence without quotes
